blocks.heading: Divisibility
lines: By 3 or 9: the digit sum is. By 4: the last two digits. By 8: the last three.
By 11: (sum of digits in odd places) − (sum in even places) is 0 or a multiple of 11.
For a number like 72, check its co-prime parts: 8 and 9.

blocks.heading: Factors
lines: Write N = p^a × q^b × r^c. N has (a + 1)(b + 1)(c + 1) factors.
Odd factors: leave out the power of 2. Even factors: total − odd.

blocks.heading: HCF and LCM
lines: HCF takes the lowest power of each prime, LCM the highest.
For two numbers: HCF × LCM = the product of the numbers.
"Leaves remainder r when divided by a, b and c": the number is a multiple of LCM(a, b, c), plus r.

blocks.heading: Remainders and last digits
lines: The remainder of a product is the product of the remainders, reduced again.
Look for a power that leaves remainder 1: 2³ = 8 leaves 1 on division by 7, so 2⁹⁹ does too.
Last digits repeat every 4 powers: 2, 4, 8, 6 for 2; 3, 9, 7, 1 for 3; 7, 9, 3, 1 for 7; 8, 4, 2, 6 for 8.
Last digit of 7⁴²: 42 leaves 2 on division by 4, so it's the 2nd in the cycle, 9.

blocks.heading: Factorials and counting
lines: Trailing zeros in n!: n ÷ 5 + n ÷ 25 + n ÷ 125 + ..., whole parts only. 100! has 20 + 4 = 24.
Numbers up to N divisible by a or b: N ÷ a + N ÷ b − N ÷ LCM(a, b), whole parts only.

blocks.heading: Traps
lines: 1 is neither prime nor composite. 2 is the only even prime.
Natural numbers start at 1. Check whether 0 or negative numbers are allowed.
With digit questions, write the number as 10a + b and keep a from 1 to 9.
